hook: An unfinished Foundation site has relocated three kilometers north by itself, and something inside it is still running containment. The core of the article is the paperwork those inhabitants have been producing, which is both funnier and more disturbing than the official sections around it.
whyItMatters: 1312 holds a mirror up to the SCP format, seen through creatures that copy Foundation routines without understanding them. Its three colors of featureless figures sort neatly into roles a reader will recognize: white ones that direct experiments and write reports, black ones that capture intruders and shout about breaches, and orange ones that only move when told. The result is a parody of containment reduced to its bare gestures: box it, lock it, guard it, test it, recite the motto.
thingsToNotice: The recovered documents copy the format with childlike literalism: an orange stick with blackness inside, apparently a pen, kills a D-class who swallows it, is cut back out of his neck, and goes through five experiments logged as wet, cold, warm, silent and broken. The second document, about a cylinder of something that has gone cold, collapses into pages calling a doctor a liar, his name scraped off the paper apparently by a fingernail. The third concerns the expedition member caught on the way out: a pink man in tough material who insists he works for the Foundation, whose gun they tested on D-class and whose radio kept asking for Agent Banks. They lock him up, feed him D-class, hit him if he tries to escape, and run the same five tests, which now end in a splash, shivering, lies and, after the cutting, the single word wet. The class line at the top already reads Keter Neutralized.
